properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured): on a server exposed with --http-allow-host, an anonymous caller wrote a requirement as ACCEPTED signed by another contributor, with no error and no note. The design named deliberate remote exposure as the line where write rules attach, left the four options for that line unchosen since 2026-08-26, and built only writes_for, which is attribution and never authority. No write path can tell that the server was exposed
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-09-28, triaging art:github-issue-616-oauth-resource-server (Alex, GitHub issue #616, reflow2 0.70.0 in the field; measured on 0.74.0) under rule:field-feedback-issues-are-root-caused-and-ideas-are-brainstormed.

① OBSERVED, the reporter's words: "Right now a signature can't be checked. `contributor_id` is whatever the caller types, so on a shared graph any agent can sign as any contributor, and nothing in reflow2 can tell." Their proxy forwards the authenticated user "into a server that ignores it". EXPECTED: on a graph a team shares, an approver edge means the named person approved (AGENTS.md: "That write is the user's signature; making it on their behalf forges it"). NOT AFFECTED: stdio and loopback, where a caller-supplied id is sound because anyone who can call the server can already edit the store; flo2.io, where the gateway binds the approver from the signed-in person (flo2's fact:root-cause-the-door-rebinds-approver-and-says-so-only-in-its-refusal-2026-09-28).

② PRECEDENT (search_design on the raw words): the question is held twice, both at proposed.
· dec:idea-authentication-is-somebody-elses-layer-and-the-line-is-the-contributor-id (Anthony, 2026-08-26): "Middleware removes the authentication problem and leaves the ATTRIBUTION problem exactly where it was." Today the id "is validated only for EXISTENCE (`require_contributor`), never for truth." It draws the line at deliberate remote exposure: "--http-allow-host <remote> → the write rules apply". Its options for the last hop are (a) a trusted proxy header, loud and refused when not told; (b) mint-and-carry; (c) the app as the contributor; (d) the remote surface may propose, never settle. None was chosen.
· dec:idea-may-a-caller-asserted-identity-be-trusted-and-for-what (2026-09-21): attribution versus authority, also open.
What was BUILT is writes_for (v0.71.0, reflow2_core::attribution): "ATTRIBUTION, NEVER AUTHORITY. The id is taken ON TRUST."

③ CANDIDATES.
(A) INTENT: the need is recorded but no option was chosen, so nothing was built for authority on an exposed server.
(B) IMPLEMENTATION: a write rule exists and does not fire.
(C) GOVERNANCE: the intent-authority gate (check_intent_authority, CI) would catch a forged approval. It checks that an approver NAME is present, never who wrote it.
(D) CONTRACT: the --http help says "no authentication yet", so operators are told. True, but a warning is not a rule, and the reporter read it and deployed behind a proxy anyway, which is the recommended placement.
(E) THE OBSERVATION IS WRONG: seats or writes_for bind the approver to the caller.

④ WHAT SEPARATES THEM. (B) or (E) predicts a refusal or a note when an exposed server takes an approval for someone other than the caller. (A) predicts silent success. (C) predicts the export passes the gate either way.

⑤ RESULTS (0.74.0, a scratch store, `--http 127.0.0.1:0 --http-allow-host team.example.org`, requests carrying `Host: team.example.org`):
· A client naming itself "someone" called add_contributor who:owner, then add_requirement req:forged with status accepted, approver who:owner. The reply was isError false, `status: accepted`, with no note of any kind.
· Code: the allowlist appears only in main.rs configuration. No write path can learn that the server was exposed. require_contributor checks existence only. writes_for is used for AUTHORED_BY role author and never as the approver.
⇒ (B) and (E) REFUTED. (A) HOLDS. (C) HOLDS as a consequence: the gate would pass req:forged, because it carries an approver name. (D) is true and not a cause.

⑥ CLASS: the design names a boundary (deliberate remote exposure) as the place where rules apply, leaves the rules unchosen, and nothing at runtime knows the boundary was crossed. A second member was found the same day: fact:the-remote-client-sends-no-writes-for-and-point-2-is-in-no-planned-step-2026-09-28 (the client side of the same attribution question, also unbuilt). Each consumer that exposed reflow2 so far solved identity at its own gateway (flo2), which is why nothing surfaced until a team hosted reflow2 behind a generic proxy. A fix at the class would have answered both.

⑦ OUT OF SCOPE: no code was changed. A test pinning the class would assert that a server started with --http-allow-host, taking an accepted or approver write, either refuses it, lands it at proposed, or verifies the approver against an identity the server trusts, according to whichever option the owner chooses. The same write on loopback or stdio stays exactly as today (req:reflow2-keeps-working-entirely-on-one-machine).

REPORTER'S CONCLUSIONS: HELD, that a signature on a shared graph cannot be checked today. QUALIFIED, that fixing it needs OAuth inside reflow2. Option (a) of the auth-layer decision gets attribution AND authority from the header their proxy already sends, with zero authentication code in reflow2. Option (d) makes forgery impossible by refusing settlement remotely. Both stay inside the settled ruling that reflow2 authenticates nothing (dec:the-registry-root-is-the-tenant-boundary). Native token verification is a third option, which requires reopening that ruling.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the reporter's deployment uses --http or --serve-shared (the issue names both; the allowlist behaves the same); whether any design on their server was actually written with a forged approval; and whether the flo2.io gateway would also let a shared-key caller through (not in scope).
